newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DTB changes margins on some derivatives.
newsitem.headline: German DTB changes margins on some derivatives.

text.p: Deutsche Terminboerse, the German futures and options exchange, on Wednesday announced it will change margins for some of its derivative products on Thursday, March 27.
The exchange said in a statement it was reducing its margin requirement on the Bund futures contract and on the option on the contract to 1.4 points from 1.5 points or to 3,500 marks from 3,750.
The margin requirement on the five-year bond future or Bundesobligationen (Bobl) future will fall to 1.0 point from 1.2 points or to 2,500 marks from 3,000 marks.
The margin requirement on options on the DAX share index and on the DAX future will rise to 150 points from 120 or to 15,000 marks from 12,000 marks.
The margin on the MDAX futures contract will rise to 120 points from 100 points or to 1,200 marks from 1,000.
